subject: Hospitality
title: Water Conservation by Design
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Water Conservation by Design.

hook.text: A luxury hotel guest uses 200+ liters of water daily—bathing, pools, laundry, landscaping.

buildup.text: Low-flow fixtures, rainwater harvesting, greywater recycling, and drought-resistant landscaping cut water use by 30–40%.

discovery.text: Greywater systems reuse sink and shower water for toilet flushing and irrigation. One guest's shower waters tomorrow's garden.

twist.text: The biggest water user isn't the guest—it's laundry. Hotels asking guests to reuse towels save millions of liters annually.

climax.text: In water-scarce destinations like the Maldives or Dubai, water conservation isn't optional.

punchline.text: Reuse the towel, recycle the shower. Every drop saved is money and planet preserved.
